page: Amazon Web Services r8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, the instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration features an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside 32.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 7 GHz, establishing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, does not provision integrated local storage, and includes zero hardware acceleration GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation shows balanced single-thread compute efficiency offset by constrained aggregate throughput. The instance achieves competitive results in single-threaded tasks, scoring 1890.0 in Geekbench single-core and 33.41 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside strong text processing performance at 2742.0. However, multi-core scaling is naturally restricted by the 2 physical core count, registering 4363.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 4286.46 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 31.47 GB/sec for reads and 17.95 GB/sec for writes, reflecting standard tier memory throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.xlarge provides economical access to DDR5 memory capacity and modern Intel instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AMX matrix extensions, without requiring large core allocations. Because there is no bundled local NVMe storage, workloads rely exclusively on remote EBS storage volumes. The profile fits in-memory caching solutions like Redis, which sustained 7.49 million SET operations per second, intermediate relational database servers, memory-bound data filtering, and single-threaded data compression tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor on x86_64 architecture at 3.9 GHz. Managed through the Nitro hypervisor, the server delivers 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) backed by a 480 MB L3 cache. It operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, has no local instance storage, and includes no GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate capable single-core execution, marked by 33.41 GB/sec gzip compression throughput and a 1890.0 Geekbench single-core score, while multi-core compute throughput reflects the 2-core boundary. In-memory execution is steady, demonstrated by 7.49 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides resource-efficient memory capacity for memory-resident key-value stores, intermediate transactional databases, lightweight web serving, and compression-intensive applications.
